metadata.note: Same composition as the lamellar check: f = 0.56, chiN = 12, on the hexagonal cell.

assumptions: Human and AI requests use the same validation and the same solver.
client is provenance only. It does not change the calculation.
No parameter was rewritten to force a result.
PSCF diblock examples use block lengths that sum to 1. The adapter writes χN into the chi entry and does not pass a separate N.
Monomer concentrations were written with WRITE_C_RGRID after ITERATE. That does not change the free energy. A missing grid is not filled in.
Only the requested example cells are compared. A lower fHelmholtz is preferred only among cells that converged.
Space-group names in the result are the vendored example identities, not a symmetry calculated for this composition.

method.source: University of Minnesota PSCF (pscf_rpc), not the 1D prototype

solver_assumptions: PSCF diblock examples use block lengths that sum to 1. The adapter writes χN into the chi entry and does not pass a separate N.
Initial fields are the vendored PSCF example fields (lam, hex, gyr, bcc).
The reported morphology is the converged cell with the lowest fHelmholtz.
PSCF source is third_party/pscfpp, GPL-3.0-or-later, copyright 2015-2026 The Regents of the University of Minnesota.
The copied PSCF command writes the monomer concentration after ITERATE. That file is the field PSCF computed. It is not an atomistic structure.

interpretation.calculated: Among the tested morphologies that converged, hexagonal cylinders has the lowest fHelmholtz.
interpretation.prediction: Within this PSCF model and among the tested morphologies, the calculation predicts hexagonal cylinders. That is a model prediction, not a statement that the morphology will form.
interpretation.experimental: Hexagonal cylinders is a candidate for experimental investigation if the composition, segregation strength, and processing are comparable to this calculation. The model does not account for kinetic trapping, molecular-weight distribution, solvent history, temperature history, or defects. The prediction requires experimental validation.
interpretation.limitations: This is a calculation inside the selected model. It does not include dispersity, processing, solvent history, defects, or a measured temperature. Experimental validation is required.

visualization.reason: Monomer concentrations from PSCF WRITE_C_RGRID. Passing them to visualize writes an Avogadro CJSON volume, not an atomistic file.
